solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: His Excellency joining newly-weds in Scottish isles

parts.note: HE is the standard abbreviation for His Excellency, an ambassador's title
brides are women who have just married, newly-weds

explanation.surface: An ambassador joins a honeymooning couple on a trip to the Scottish islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrides are the island chains off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Spanish hero extremely equivocal with detectives

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters, so only the outside of equivocal is used

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: A Spanish champion is found to be very evasive when questioned by police.
explanation.definitionFit: El Cid was the medieval Castilian warrior celebrated as Spain's national champion.

clue.text: Learn something new about coach

parts.note: re is a Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning
to coach someone is to train them

explanation.surface: Someone picks up a new skill on the subject of coaching.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrain is to undergo fresh instruction, acquiring new skills for another job.

clue.text: Cheat on husband? What an idiot I am!

parts.note: to do someone is slang for to swindle or cheat them
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy and marriage records

explanation.surface: Someone who has been unfaithful to their spouse realises their own folly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doh is the exclamation, popularised by Homer Simpson, made on realising one's own stupidity.

clue.text: Hurry up and fix gas leak, eh?

indicators.note: to fix something can mean to rig or rearrange it, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A plea to the plumber to get on with repairing a gas leak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fix' reads as repairing the leak, but it signals that GASLEAKEH is to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Shake a leg is an informal idiom urging someone to move faster.

clue.text: Two parties that never got off the ground?

definitions.text: Two parties that never got off the ground?

indicators.note: two of the same thing means the single word is written twice in a row

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Two parties that were planned but never actually took place.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: two parties side by side build the word, and 'never got off the ground' turns those flops into a bird that could not fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo was a flightless bird of Mauritius, so it literally never left the ground.

clue.text: Language spoken by a Cockney's wife?

definitions.meaning: in Cockney slang 'my old ...' means my wife, from duchess

explanation.surface: Asking what tongue an East Londoner's spouse speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner from the East End; 'my old Dutch' is their traditional term for a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutch names both the Netherlands' tongue and, in old London slang, a man's spouse.

clue.text: Send insane, angered terribly

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly or wildly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone so furious it has driven them mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to drive someone mad or unbalance their mind.

clue.text: Quash spirit of the Highlands?

definitions.meaning: to ... a rumour or plan is to put an end to it
Whisky, the spirit distilled in Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone suppresses the proud character of the Scottish highlanders.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch means both to stamp out and the whisky made in Scotland.

clue.text: In Zermatt I repack clothes

indicators.note: in says the answer is sitting inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A skier in the Swiss resort of Zermatt repacks a suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: Attire is a formal word for the garments a person wears.

clue.text: Thought to be perfect but coming up short?

indicators.note: falling short means lacking the final part, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: Something thought perfect but which in fact fails to deliver.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a notion or something conceived in the mind.

clue.text: Help net a surprisingly large creature

indicators.note: surprisingly hints that the letters end up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A huge animal is caught in a net with help, to everyone's astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The elephant is the largest living land animal.

clue.text: I line team up for murder

indicators.note: up can mean in disorder, as in things being mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gangster lines up a team to carry out a killing.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate someone is a euphemism for killing them.

clue.text: Beach where one meets 007?

parts.note: 007 is the code number of the fictional spy James Bond
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Asking at which seaside spot you might bump into James Bond.
explanation.walkthrough: Bondi Beach is a famous surfing beach in Sydney, Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Bondi is Sydney's best-known stretch of sand by the Pacific.

clue.text: Storm created by anger in pub?

parts.note: a bar is a place serving drinks, a pub
rage means anger

explanation.surface: A tempest of shouting breaks out from fury in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a storm or torrent, as of questions or gunfire.

clue.text: LSE admitting reactionary old man's mistake

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so one piece goes inside the other
reactionary suggests going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: pa is an informal word for one's father, the old man

explanation.surface: The London School of Economics takes in a right-wing father who has made an error.
explanation.walkthrough: LSE is the London School of Economics, a university college. 'reactionary' is the reversal signal, not a political jibe.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or minor error, a momentary failing.

clue.text: Might this indicate a dog?

parts.note: the thing that indicates is a needle or arrow, and it is also a gundog breed that indicates game

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a sign points out where a dog is.
explanation.walkthrough: The word works both ways: something that indicates, and a hunting dog that stands still to indicate game.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer is both an indicating needle and a breed of gundog.

clue.text: Understanding how Scrooge might be described?

explanation.surface: Coming to understand the character of Dickens's famous miser.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasping means both comprehending and greedy, as the miserly Ebenezer Scrooge is.

clue.text: Rotter having success in Home Counties

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: SE, south-east, stands for the Home Counties, the counties around London
a win is a success

explanation.surface: A cad prospering in the wealthy commuter belt around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties surrounding London, in the south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: Swine is an insult for a contemptible person, as rotter is.

clue.text: Couple I encountered on way back

indicators.note: on the way back means going in reverse, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: met means encountered

explanation.surface: Someone recalls meeting a pair while returning home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on way back' is the reversal signal and applies only to the word for encountered, not to I.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is an informal term for a romantic couple.

clue.text: Former wife going to Ascot occasionally? That's correct

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: An ex-wife attends Royal Ascot races now and then, and that's right.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is an English racecourse, famous for its fashionable royal meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precise or accurate, that is right.

clue.text: Posh princess in cheap car

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: the Lada is a budget Russian car make
Di is short for Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A grand princess rides in a budget car.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da describes affected, pretentiously upper-class manners.

clue.text: Giant welcoming island painter

indicators.note: welcoming means taking someone in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a titan is a giant

explanation.surface: A huge figure greeting a famous artist on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was the great Venetian Renaissance artist.

clue.text: Get even with chap from Bangkok, did you say?

indicators.note: asking what you said indicates the answer sounds like a word, not spelt like it

parts.note: a man from Bangkok, the capital of Thailand, is a Thai

explanation.surface: Settling the score with a man from Bangkok.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie is to finish level, drawing with an opponent.

clue.text: Two chaps who'll make you giggle?

definitions.text: Two chaps who'll make you giggle?

indicators.note: two of the same thing means the single word is written twice in a row

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a chap, a man

explanation.surface: A pair of men known for making people laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: two chaps side by side build the word, and that word is itself the sound of a giggle.
explanation.definitionFit: He-he imitates the sound of a titter or chuckle.

clue.text: Curse West Country river case

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, in England's West Country
a crate is a packing case

explanation.surface: Swearing at a box found by a river in the south-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Country is south-west England: Devon, Cornwall, Somerset and nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or call down damnation on someone.
